summary: Donald E. Gjertson is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Stanford University (~1969–1975) under Akira Takeda and John Ching-yu Wang, and held a post at the University of Massachusetts Amherst (~1976–2010).

Donald K. Swearer is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He held posts at Swarthmore College (~1970–2004) and Harvard University (2004–2010), where he was a Distinguished Visiting Fellow at the Center for the Study of World Religions.

Donald Keene (1922–2019) was a Japanologist who studied at Columbia University (~1938–1951) under Wm. Theodore de Bary and at Harvard University (~1946–1947). He held posts at the University of Cambridge (1949–1954) and Columbia University (1955).

Donald Phillip Verene is a philosopher who studied at Knox College (~1955–1959) and Washington University in St. Louis (~1959–1964). He served as chair at Emory University (1982–1988) and held visiting posts at Pembroke College (1988) and Sapienza University of Rome (1996).
Donald R. Davis Jr. is an Indologist. He studied under Richard W. Lariviere, Patrick Olivelle (attested 2005), and Ludo Rocher.

Donald S. Lopez Jr. is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his BA, MA, and PhD at the University of Virginia (~1970–1982) under Jeffrey Hopkins, later holding professorial posts at Middlebury College (1986) and the University of Michigan (1990).

id: P:Dong Kam Tulku Ngawang Damchö Gyatso
summary: Dong Kam Tulku Ngawang Damchö Gyatso studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Dongak Chokyi Nyima studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Dongak Tendzin studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and also taught Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Dongchu (1908–1977) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Minnan Buddhist Academy (~1929–1933) and under Taixu, Aiting, and Nanting. He was abbot of Dinghui Temple (~1945–1949) and held posts at Jiaoshan Buddhist Institute and Jing'an Temple Buddhist Academy.

Dongmei Fang (1899–1977) was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Nanking, under John Dewey, and at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1921–1923), later holding posts at National Central University (1925–1948) and National Taiwan University (~1948–1973).

Donna C. Kurtz is an archaeology and history scholar. She studied at Yale University, the University of Cincinnati, and Somerville College, Oxford (~1965–1968), and held a post at the Classical Art Research Centre (~1970–2011).

Dor Bahadur Bista is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields who studied at Tri-Chandra Multiple Campus. He was a professor at Tribhuvan University (~1978–1990) and served on the board of governors of the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development.
Doranne Jacobson is an Indologist who earned a doctorate in anthropology from Columbia University. She held a post at Columbia University as a seminar associate at the Southern Asian Institute.

Doris Meth Srinivasan is a scholar of Indology and archaeology. After earning a BA at Hunter College and a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania, she held posts at Columbia, Barnard, George Washington, George Mason, and the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art.
Doris Unterthurner is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned an MA at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Dorje Rinchen (1819–1867) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Sakya Yab Jé Kün Ga Rinchen, Ja Shong Lob Zur Lodrö Gyatso, Nying Ri Tri Chen Tutob Tendzin, Chime Tenpai Nyima, and Sakya Dak Chen Ngawang Kün Ga Gyaltsen.

Dorje Tseten (1925–2013) was a Tibetology and history scholar who earned an education degree at Beijing Normal University (-1948). He served as director of the China Tibetology Research Center from 1986 to 2000.

Dorji Banzarov (1822–1855) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. He studied at the First Kazan Male Gymnasium and Kazan Imperial University (~1842–1846) under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski, as well as the école militaire russo-mongole.

Dorji Wangchuk is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute and the University of Hamburg (~1998–2005) under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, becoming a professor at the University of Hamburg in 2009.
